# War Scroll Column 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 16 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**1** [...] the priests shall blow on the trumpets [...] for the arrangement of the battle lines [...]

**2** [...] and on the trumpets of assembly they shall blow a sustained note for the directing of the battle [...]

**3** [...they shall begin] to fell the slain. And all the people shall cease the war cry, but the priests shall continue to blow

**4** on the trumpets of the slain to direct the battle, until the enemy is struck down and they turn

**5** in retreat. And the priests shall blow to direct the battle. And when they are defeated

**6** before them, the priests shall blow the trumpets of assembly, and all the front-line infantry shall go out

**7** to them from among the fallen of the front ranks, and six divisions shall take their stand. And the division going out

**8** with its battle equipment shall station itself at its assigned position. And six further divisions shall take position,

**9** all of them together numbering twenty-six divisions. And the cavalry on the right and on the left

**10** of the battle line shall stand: six hundred on the one side and six hundred on the other.

**11** And when Belial girds himself to come to the aid of the Sons of Darkness, and the slain among the infantry begin to fall

**12** through the mysteries of God, testing all those appointed for battle — the priests

**13** shall blow the trumpets of summoning for another battle line to go forth as a replacement force

**14** [...] and the priests shall blow for them the signals to draw up the ranks [...]

**15** [...] and with the sounding of the priests [...] to test through these mysteries [...all those appointed]

**16** for the battle [...] and the warriors of [...] the war [...] the God of Israel [...]

**17** [...] for all the appointed seasons of eternity [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 16 preserves tactical instructions for the final phases of engagement. Significant lacunae in lines 1-3 and 14-17. "Mysteries" renders Hebrew raz in its distinctive Qumran theological sense. Line divisions follow Yadin's standard edition.*
